### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.bufremove

### Description

I feel like some buffer utility command will be usefull in mini module. Here's what I have got. Purely vibecoded though:
```lua
-- utils/buf.lua
-- :BD [pat...] [!pat...]  -- delete buffers matching pat, excluding !pat
-- go / [count]go          -- ls + :buffer prompt / ls + :BD prompt
-- ZB / [count]ZB          -- close current buffer (mercy: refuse if modified, unless count given)
-- ZO / [count]ZO          -- close all other buffers (confirm if modified, unless count given)
-- <M-n>                   -- switch to an empty scratch buffer (or create one)

local fn, api = vim.fn, vim.api
local M = {}

-- Every listed buffer, optionally narrowed by `pred(buf)`.
local function listed_bufs(pred)
  return vim
    .iter(api.nvim_list_bufs())
    :filter(function(b)
      return vim.bo[b].buflisted and (pred == nil or pred(b))
    end)
    :totable()
end

local function lastused(b)
  return fn.getbufinfo(b)[1].lastused
end

-- bufnr, glob, file name, or tail name
local function matches(buf, pat)
  if tonumber(pat) then
    return tonumber(pat) == buf
  end
  local name = api.nvim_buf_get_name(buf)
  local tail = fn.fnamemodify(name, ':t')
  if pat:find '[*?[]' then
    local rp = fn.glob2regpat(pat)
    return fn.match(name, rp) ~= -1 or fn.match(tail, rp) ~= -1
  end
  return tail == pat or name == pat or name == fn.fnamemodify(pat, ':p')
end

local function any_match(buf, pats)
  return vim.iter(pats):any(function(p)
    return matches(buf, p)
  end)
end

-- show an untouched empty buffer if one exists, else create one
local function buf_new()
  local shown = fn.tabpagebuflist()
  local empty = listed_bufs(function(b)
    return api.nvim_buf_get_name(b) == '' and vim.bo[b].buftype == '' and api.nvim_buf_get_changedtick(b) <= 2 and not vim.list_contains(shown, b)
  end)[1]
  vim.cmd(empty and 'buffer ' .. empty or 'enew')
end

-- move the current window off the buffers in `bufs`: alt buffer, else MRU, else empty
local function switch_away(bufs)
  local target = fn.bufnr '#'
  if fn.buflisted(target) ~= 1 or vim.list_contains(bufs, target) then
    local shown = fn.tabpagebuflist()
    local cand = listed_bufs(function(b)
      return not vim.list_contains(bufs, b)
        and not vim.list_contains(shown, b)
        and (vim.bo[b].buftype == '' or vim.bo[b].buftype == 'help')
        and not (vim.bo[b].modified and vim.bo[b].readonly)
    end)
    table.sort(cand, function(a, b)
      return lastused(a) > lastused(b)
    end)
    target = cand[1]
  end
  if target then
    vim.cmd('buffer ' .. target)
  else
    buf_new()
  end
end

-- returns false if the user cancelled
local function confirm_save(buf)
  local ok, choice = pcall(fn.confirm, ('Save changes to %q?'):format(fn.bufname(buf)), '&Yes\n&No\n&Cancel')
  if ok and choice == 1 then
    api.nvim_buf_call(buf, vim.cmd.write)
  end
  return ok and (choice == 1 or choice == 2)
end

-- force = true skips the "save changes?" prompt and discards edits.
local function delete_bufs(bufs, force)
  for _, buf in ipairs(bufs) do
    if api.nvim_buf_is_valid(buf) and (force or not vim.bo[buf].modified or confirm_save(buf)) then
      for _, win in ipairs(fn.win_findbuf(buf)) do
        api.nvim_win_call(win, function()
          switch_away(bufs)
        end)
      end
      local name = fn.bufname(buf)
      if name ~= '' then
        pcall(vim.cmd, 'argdelete ' .. fn.fnameescape(name))
      end
      pcall(vim.cmd, 'bdelete! ' .. buf)
    end
  end
end

--- API (usable without calling setup) ------------------------------------

--- Delete buffer(s): a bufnr, a list of bufnrs, or nil/0 for the current one.
---@param bufs? integer|integer[]
---@param force? boolean discard changes without prompting
function M.delete(bufs, force)
  if not bufs or bufs == 0 then
    bufs = api.nvim_get_current_buf()
  end
  delete_bufs(type(bufs) == 'number' and { bufs } or bufs, force)
end

function M.other(force)
  local cur = api.nvim_get_current_buf()
  delete_bufs(
    listed_bufs(function(b)
      return b ~= cur
    end),
    force
  )
end

M.list = listed_bufs
M.new = buf_new

--- commands + keymaps ----------------------------------------------------

function M.setup()
  api.nvim_create_user_command('BD', function(o)
    local inc, exc = {}, {}
    for _, arg in ipairs(o.fargs) do
      local bang, pat = arg:match '^(!?)(.*)'
      if pat == '%' or pat == '#' then
        pat = fn.bufnr(pat)
      end
      table.insert(bang == '!' and exc or inc, pat)
    end

    local targets = listed_bufs(function(b)
      if any_match(b, exc) then
        return false
      end
      if #inc > 0 then
        return any_match(b, inc)
      end
      return #exc > 0
    end)

    delete_bufs(targets)
    vim.notify(('BD: removed %d, remaining: %d'):format(#targets, #listed_bufs()), vim.log.levels.WARN)
  end, { nargs = '*', complete = 'buffer' })

  vim.keymap.set('n', 'go', function()
    return ':<c-u>set nomore<bar>ls<bar>set more<cr>:' .. (vim.v.count > 0 and 'BD' or 'buffer') .. '<space>'
  end, { expr = true })

  vim.keymap.set('n', 'ZB', function()
    if vim.v.count == 0 and vim.bo.modified then
      return vim.notify 'buffer has unsaved changes (use "[count]ZB" to discard changes)'
    end
    M.delete(0, vim.v.count > 0)
  end)

  vim.keymap.set('n', 'ZO', function()
    local before = #listed_bufs()
    M.other(vim.v.count > 0)
    vim.notify((before - #listed_bufs()) .. ' buffer(s) deleted')
  end)

  vim.keymap.set('n', '<M-n>', buf_new)
end

return M
```
Btw, the bufkillmercy and buf_new part is taken from venerable justinmk. But the `BD` command is from claude

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the suggestion and a prototype!

I think this is a bit out of scope for 'mini.bufremove'. Its utilities can be combined with other modules (like 'mini.pick' buffer picker) or built-in functionalities (like `:bufdo`), but having something more is probably too much.
I feel it would have nice as a mini.extra utils, but I can see keeping the plugin lean also important.
